Confirmed via computed styles + visual screenshot that 'Área do Candidato' button and top navigation menu (INÍCIO/CONTRATE-NOS/INTEGRIDADE) are now HIDDEN on mobile (#TopLogin and #TopMenu computed display:none). Body/html overflow-x:hidden works (bodyScrollW == viewportWidth, no horizontal overflow). VLibras hidden. HOWEVER, two visible bugs remain across ALL 6 pages: (a) #Topo has ~400px of empty blue space because a later CSS rule '#Topo{height:400px!important;width:780px!important;margin-bottom:20px!important}' overrides the injected mobile-fix media-query rule (equal CSS specificity + equal !important => later rule wins). (b) Logo is left-aligned (not centered) because '#Logo{float:left;width:200px;margin-right:20px}' plus '#Logo{margin-top:20px}' from base CSS are not overridden by the media query (same specificity issue). action_items: In the injected <style id='__mobile_header_fix'> block, increase CSS specificity so it wins over the base later rules. Options: (1) use body-scoped selectors: 'body #Topo{...}' and 'body #Topo #Logo{...}'; OR (2) move the injected <style> block to the END of <head> AND explicitly override height/width/float/margin-top/margin-right. Concretely add to the @media(max-width:768px) block: 'body #Topo{height:auto !important; min-height:0 !important; width:100% !important; max-width:100vw !important; margin-bottom:0 !important; padding:8px 0 !important} body #Topo #Logo{float:none !important; width:100% !important; max-width:100% !important; margin:0 !important; text-align:center !important} body #Topo #Logo h1{width:auto !important; margin:0 auto !important; text-align:center !important}'.
Apply the same fix to all 6 public HTMLs: inicio.html, inscricao.html, confirmacao.html, inscricao-realizada.html, pagamento-pix.html, termos.html.
critical_code_review_comments: Injecting a <style> block to override existing CSS should always use higher-specificity selectors (e.g., prefixed with 'body' or 'html') when there are LATER unconditional !important rules in the same document. Media queries alone do NOT boost specificity.

Base HTML has redundant/conflicting #Topo rules ('#Topo{background:#fff;height:200px}' followed later by '#Topo{margin-bottom:20px!important;height:400px!important;width:780px!important}'). The 780px fixed width is inherently mobile-incompatible; consider removing height/width on #Topo and letting it flex to content.

rca of the issue: CSS specificity/order problem. The injected mobile-fix media query rule and the later unconditional rule '#Topo{height:400px!important;width:780px!important;margin-bottom:20px!important}' both use the '#Topo' selector (specificity 0,1,0,0) with !important. Per CSS cascade, when specificity and importance tie, source order decides — and the LATER rule wins. Media queries don't affect specificity or ordering; they only gate whether a rule applies. Fix: prefix the injected mobile rules with 'body ' (or 'html body ') to raise specificity to 0,1,0,1, defeating the later 0,1,0,0 rule regardless of source order. Additionally, must explicitly set height:auto !important (or min-height:0) on #Topo in the mobile rule to negate the forced 400px height.
